The petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.745/2008, on the file of Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Thodupuzha is the appellant herein.
The respondents in the O.P. are the respondents herein.

2. The petitioner filed the above claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 30.07.2008.

According to the petitioner, on 30.07.2008 at 3 P.M., while he was standing by the side of the Kattappana - Thodupuzha road in front of Prince Bakery, a car bearing Reg. No. KL-5-Q-8613 driven by the 1st respondent along the said road in a rash and negligent manner and excessive speed knocked him down and thereby he sustained injuries.
Immediately he was taken to District Hospital, Painavu and he was treated as inpatient there till 11.08.2008.
Thereafter, he underwent further treatment at the Chazhikattu Hospital, Thodupuzha.
3. According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the car by MACA NO. 2498 OF 2013 2024:KER:95347 the 1st respondent.
4. The 2nd respondent is the owner and the 3 rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
5. Therefore, he filed the claim petition claiming a total compensation of Rs.13,00,000/-.
6. Respondent Nos. 1 & 2 remained ex parte.
The 3rd respondent filed a written statement admitting the accident as well as the valid policy.
However, it is contented that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner.

sentences.text: The evidence in the case consists of Exts. A11 to A17.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

After evaluating the evidence, the Tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs.2,82,785/-
aggrieved by the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, he preferred this appeal.

8. Now, the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
MACA NO. 2498 OF 2013 2024:KER:95347 9.
Heard Sri. A.K. Gopalan, the learned counsel for the appellant and Sri. P. Jacob Mathew, the learned counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10. The point:
Though in the written statement the 3rd respondent has raised a contention that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner, no evidence was adduced by the respondents.
On the other hand, the petitioner produced copy of the final report in Crime No.236 of 2008 of Idukki Police Station as Ext.A3, and it proves the negligence of the 1st respondent.
Therefore, the 3rd respondent being the insurer is liable to indemnify the liability of the owner of the insured vehicle.
11. According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the petitioner was working as a Welder and earning Rs.250/- per day.
However, the Tribunal has fixed the income at Rs.4,500/- alone, which according to him is on the lesser side.
Though, the petitioner would claim that he was earning Rs.250/- per day, the same was not proved.

In the above circumstances, in the light of the dictum laid down by the MACA NO. 2498 OF 2013 2024:KER:95347 Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd. [(2011) 13 SCC 236], his notional income is fixed at Rs.7,500/- per month.

sentences.text: 12. The petitioner produced Ext.A8, disability certificate issued by the Standing Disability Assessment Board dated 18.09.2009, stating that he has a permanent disability of 25%.

The learned counsel would argue that, though the permanent disability show in Ext.A8 is only 25%, he is unable to perform his duties and he could not even eat his food with his right hand because of the injury sustained in the accident.

13. In the accident, the petitioner sustained laceration on right distal arm with muscle injury,
laceration of right thigh and ulnar nerve injury.

The petitioner underwent surgery (redebridement and ulnar nerve repair under brachial block)
14.

In the award of the Tribunal, noted that the petitioner appeared before the Tribunal and the Tribunal was MACA NO. 2498 OF 2013 2024:KER:95347 satisfied that his right ring finger is not moving at all.
The Tribunal also noted that the petitioner told that he cannot even eat his food with right hand.

Considering the fact that the petitioner was working as Welder and his right ring finger is not moving at all, though, his permanent physical disability is only 25%, his functional disability Vincent Mathew Alias Shaji vs Vijayan.K.K(*Expired,Lr'Simpleaded) on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40968861/

sentences.text: 3 will be much more.
It is true that the petitioner has not adduced any oral evidence in this case.

In spite of the fact that, he has not adduced any oral evidence, considering the evidence on record including Ext.A8 disability certificate and the observation made by the Tribunal in the award after personally seeing the petitioner, I hold that, for the purpose of quantifying the quantum of compensation, his functional disability can be fixed at 40%.
15. Since the deceased was aged 39, towards future prospects 40% of the income is to be added and the multiplier to be applied is 15.
Therefore, his monthly income including future prospects will come to 10500/-(7500+40% of 7500).
Accordingly, the loss due to disability will come to Rs.7,86,000/- including the loss of income for a period of four months.
Towards extra nourishment, the Tribunal has awarded only Rs.2,000/-.

The petitioner was treated as inpatient for 12 days and thereafter he had to take rest for a considerable period and therefore, I hold that compensation towards extra nourishment awarded is too meager and hence it is enhanced to Rs.10,000/-.
17. Towards pain and suffering, the Tribunal has awarded only Rs.25,000/-.

Considering the fact that the petitioner was treated as impatient for 12 days and thereafter he had to take rest for a considerable period, the compensation awarded on the above head is on lesser side and hence, it is enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/-.
No other change is required on other heads.
Therefore, the total compensation will come to Rs.8,96,000/-.

1 Extra nourishment Rs.2,000/- Rs.10,000/-

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the 3rd respondent is directed to deposit a total compensation of Rs.8,96,000/-.
(Rupees eight Lakhs ninety six thousand only)
, less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest at 8% per annum, from the date of the petition till Vincent Mathew Alias Shaji vs Vijayan.
